a1_subject: CALL statement (rules for program-name formation for a non-COBOL program)
a1_text: CALL statement (rules for program-name formation for a non-COBOL program). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for calling non-COBOL programs. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.4, CALL statement, General rule 3b)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 13 'CALL statement (rules for program-name formation for a non-COBOL program). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for calling non-COBOL programs. This item shall be documented... (14.9.4 GR3b)'. cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "If the program being called is not a COBOL program, the rules for program-name formation and for locating the program are defined by the implementor" -> OK (§14.9.4.4 3b). Calling non-COBOL programs is NOT supported: ProbeSiblingModule loads <name>.dll and requires a __CobolModule.Register() registrar, else 'not a COBOL.NET module' -> false -> EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND. Probe callfor.cob / callfor2.cob: CALL "Antlr4.Runtime.Standard" (a real foreign .NET dll in AppContext.BaseDirectory) and CALL identifier 'System.Runtime' both take ON EXCEPTION with EXCEPTION-STATUS = EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND. So the conditional obligation is NOT incurred, and CONFORMANCE.md §3 does say 'a non-COBOL element cannot be the TARGET of a CALL' (plus DOC-A.1-19 'no non-COBOL program can be declared'). PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS: there is no DOC-A.1-13 disposition row, so the register cannot see that the item is un-incurred (audit_annex_a1.py counts it in the 195), and even with a 'Not provided' row the derived 'a1-optional-not-provided' selector is keyed to requirement 'optional' and would not reach a CONDITIONALLY-REQUIRED item — no path to a closed verdict exists today (see findings: un-incurred-A.1-items-have-no-disposition-path). Umbrella kb/Work A11. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, PB1535. || code-location commentary (registrar-normalized, kb/Work PB1522): docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 (Return to a NON-COBOL activating runtime element bullet)

CONFORMANCE.md: no DOC-A.1-14 row and no mention of EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES or 'runtime resources' anywhere (grep empty). Code: EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES has a catalog entry and NO raise site on the CALL path (CallEmitter's own summary: 'EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES ... has no raise site'), so the implemented checked-resource set is EMPTY — a legitimate determination that is written nowhere (silent). Worse, one resource failure IS detected and reported under the wrong name: ProbeSiblingModule finds <name>.dll WITH a __CobolModule registrar (the program is located) and then wraps LoadFromAssemblyPath + register.Invoke in a bare catch that returns false, so a located module that cannot be loaded/initialized (BadImageFormat, missing dependency, registrar/type-initializer throw) surfaces as EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND, whereas GR3c says 'If the program is located but the resources necessary to execute the program are not available, the EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES exception condition is set to exist' (determined by reading; a failing-registrar dll was not built in this session). DIVERGES (silent + a wrong EC name when a located module fails to load). Sibling of kb/Work PB1422 (open; FUNCTION activation twin, A.1 item 89), whose body says 'The CALL twin (A.1 item 14, §14.9.4.4 GR3c) and INVOKE (A.1 item 102) should be swept the same way' but claims no CALL row — reported in findings.json as the CALL half of that mechanism. staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 24 'CLOSE statement (closing operations). This item is required. This item shall be documented... (14.9.6, CLOSE statement, General rule 3c)'. cite.py --check 14.9.6.4 "Closing operations specified by the implementor are executed" -> OK (Table 14 symbol c, 'Close file'). CONFORMANCE.md §7 line 1619 carries DOC-A.1-24: every supported physical file is GR2 category (a) Non-unit (sequential) or (d) (relative/indexed); symbol c's closing operations = flush buffered records, persist the keyed/relative store, release the OS handle, leave open mode (GR8), release file lock and record locks (GR9/§9.1.16); OS failure -> '30', connector out of open mode either way; record area keeps its last content. Code agrees, by reading: CloseByFormat looks up Table14.Cell(format, c.Category), refuses N/A and unit-structured symbols loudly, answers '42' when not open (GR1), then SharedClose (lock release) + FileConnector.Close (CloseCore flush/dispose under try; IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException -> PermanentError '30'; _openMode=false unconditionally) + NarrowHostPostures; IndexedConnector/RelativeConnector.Category = NonSequential, sequential = NonUnit. Witnesses run at pinned HEAD: dotnet test --filter CloseTable14Tests|FileStatusDisciplineTests -> 43 passed; the three goldens re-run with the built cobol -> byte-identical to .out (pb141: flush observable via CLOSE then OPEN INPUT/READ returns DATA0001; pb235_close_unit_locks: lock release). Residual edge noted, not verdict-changing: the '30'-on-OS-failure clause has no witness (verified by reading only), and FileConnector.Close maps only IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException whereas its OPEN twin also maps ArgumentException/NotSupportedException. kb/Work PB604 (open) records that this row's inventory entry was left blank after PB235 landed — this adjudication fills it; PB235 landed. a1_subject: COBOL character repertoire (if more than one encoding in a compilation group, control functions if any)
a1_text: COBOL character repertoire (if more than one encoding in a compilation group, control functions if any). Multiple encodings are optional and control functions are optional. This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support of multiple encodings in a compilation group where control functions are defined for switching between encodings. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.1.3, COBOL character repertoire)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 26 'COBOL character repertoire (if more than one encoding in a compilation group, control functions if any). Multiple encodings are optional and control functions are optional. This item is conditionally required ... This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented... (8.1.3)'. cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 "If more than one encoding is permitted in a single compilation group, the implementor shall specify the control functions or other methods used for distinguishing between encodings" -> OK (§8.1.3.2 2). Provided but documented nowhere (no DOC-A.1-26 row, no §3 text) => DIVERGES (silent). staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 29 'Compile-Time Arithmetic (Mode of arithmetic used and rules for intermediate data handling). This item is required. This item shall be documented... (7.3.6, Syntax rule 2, General rule 2)'. cite.py --check 7.3.6.3 "The implementor shall define and document which mode of arithmetic is to be used when evaluating compile-time arithmetic" -> OK (GR2); cite.py --check 7.3.6.2 "They shall also document which intermediate rounding method is used" -> OK (SR2). CONFORMANCE.md: a determination EXISTS (§3 bullet, not a DOC-A.1-29 row) and is WRONG against the code: it says 'division truncates toward the decimal precision' and calls System.Decimal a 'standard fixed-point decimal mode'. Probe ctarith.cob: 01 C7 CONSTANT AS 2 / 3 * 3 -> 2 and 01 C11 CONSTANT AS 100 / 7 * 7 -> 100; truncating division would give 1 and 99 (System.Decimal division rounds its last digit). Determination present, code differs => DIVERGES (silent; the documented rounding method is not the implemented one). OWNED: kb/Work PB1369 (open) — its title names exactly this bullet ('calls System.Decimal a standard mode, says division truncates ... names a deleted evaluator (EvalConstExpr)') — referenced, not re-reported. staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 30 'Compiler directives, compiler directive IMP (syntax rules and general rules). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for an IMP directive. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented' (cite.py --check A.1 'compiler directive IMP (syntax rules and general rules)' -> OK §A.1 30). Clauses: §7.3.3 SR9 'If the implementor defines the IMP directive, the syntax rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined' -> OK §7.3.3 9); §7.3.4 GR4 '...the general rules for that directive shall be implementor-defined' -> OK §7.3.4 4). CONFORMANCE.md: no DOC-A.1-30 row (grep of '| DOC-A.1-30 |' empty; no mention of >>IMP anywhere in the doc). Code: no grammar or preprocessor rule recognizes IMP as a compiler-directive word (grep of src for an IMP directive finds only EC-*-IMP exception names). Probe /tmp/adj/probe/imp.cob ('>>IMP SOMETHING' before IDENTIFICATION DIVISION) -> 'error COBOL0001: unexpected '>'' rc=65: the directive is not defined, and it is refused as an anonymous parse error rather than named as an undefined implementor directive. The facility the item is conditioned on is ABSENT, so the obligation is not incurred; there is, however, no recorded posture ('Not provided.') for it, and PB280 Q1's 'Not provided.' -> DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT selector covers only OPTIONAL items, not conditionally required ones - extending it is an owner call (findings: conditional-facility-absent-posture). a1_text: Computer's coded character set (characters in and encoding of computer's alphanumeric coded character set and computer's national coded character set, encoding for usage DISPLAY and usage NATIONAL). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.1.2, Computer's coded character set; 8.3.3.2, Alphanumeric literals, Syntax rule 2; 8.3.3.5, National literals, Syntax rule 2)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 31 'Computer's coded character set (characters in and encoding of computer's alphanumeric coded character set and computer's national coded character set, encoding for usage DISPLAY and usage NATIONAL). This item is required. This item shall be documented'. §8.1.2: 'The implementor shall specify the set of characters in and the encoding of each of the computer's alphanumeric character set and the computer's national character set' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-31 |' row. Fragments of an answer live in other items' rows: DOC-A.1-33/-188 ('Both native repertoires are UTF-16, one code unit per character position'), DOC-A.1-209 ('One byte per character position' for USAGE DISPLAY), DOC-A.1-213 (2 bytes national). Those fragments are MUTUALLY INCONSISTENT for characters above U+00FF: probe /tmp/adj/probe/cs1.cob - 01 A PIC X(3) VALUE '€é' holds U+20AC in memory (ORD(A(1:1)) = 8365, DISPLAY prints '€é'), FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(A)=3, but the storage image CONVERT(A ANY ANUM HEX) = '3FE920' (€ -> 0x3F via ByteSub), and a sequential file writes it as '?' with no status (PB690, SequentialConnector Latin-1). So the code fixes a behavior (UTF-16 repertoire in memory, Latin-1 one-byte encoding at every byte boundary) and no row states the alphanumeric set's characters or its encoding. Harm: silent. a1_subject: Computer's coded character set (for literals, correspondence between compile-time and runtime character sets, when conve
a1_text: Computer's coded character set (for literals, correspondence between compile-time and runtime character sets, when conversion takes place). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon there being a difference between the compile-time and runtime computer's coded character sets. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.1.2, Computer's coded character set)

staged_record.notes: Rule: A.1 item 34 'Computer's coded character set (for literals, correspondence between compile-time and runtime character sets, when conversion takes place). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon there being a difference between the compile-time and runtime computer's coded character sets. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.1.2: 'The implementor shall define the correspondence of each character of the compile-time coded character set with an associated character in the runtime coded character set' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). Code: the compile-time computer's coded character set (the set 'used in the memory of the computer during compilation', §8.1.2 first sentence) is the .NET UTF-16 string the source is decoded into by CompilationInputs.ReadAllText; literals are emitted as C# string literals and the runtime alphanumeric/national sets are the same UTF-16 code units, so NO compile-time->runtime conversion exists (probe cs1.cob: VALUE '€é' -> ORD 8365 at run time, i.e. the compile-time character unchanged). The condition the item is conditioned on (a difference between the sets) does not arise; the facility is absent. CONFORMANCE.md states neither the identity nor the absence (no DOC-A.1-34 row), and PB690 (open) already names 'DOC-A.1-31/-34 rows' as owed - though PB690's file-encoding question is really item 31's, not item 34's (item 34 is literals only). Recorded NOT-IMPLEMENTED (facility absent) pending an owner-level posture for conditional items whose condition is unmet (finding conditional-facility-absent-posture).
